title: The orthogonalized quadratic Wick Krylov direction has an unavoidable eighth-chaos component of full variance scale

quadratic_krylov_direction.notation: Write V_N=I_4(f_N), sigma_N^2=4!||f_N||^2, X_N=V_N/sigma_N and mu_N=E(X_N^3)
quadratic_krylov_direction.product_formula: V_N^2=sum_(r=0)^4 r! binom(4,r)^2 I_(8-2r)(sym(f_N tensor_r f_N))
quadratic_krylov_direction.orthogonal_residual: R_N=X_N^2-1-mu_N X_N is orthogonal to both 1 and X_N; put tau_N^2=||R_N||_2^2 and Y_N=R_N/tau_N
quadratic_krylov_direction.top_chaos_survives: Projection onto span{1,X_N} changes only chaos zero and one direction in chaos four, so P_8 R_N=P_8(X_N^2)
quadratic_krylov_direction.normalized_lower_bound: Therefore tau_N^2=E(X_N^4)-1-mu_N^2>=1 and the normalized direction Y_N exists for every cutoff
quadratic_krylov_direction.multiplication_coupling: In the orthonormal basis {1,X_N,Y_N}, multiplication by X_N has entries <1,X_N X_N>=1 and <X_N,X_N Y_N>=tau_N>=1
quadratic_krylov_direction.ceiling: This is a finite-cutoff Gaussian-chaos statement. It supplies a new variational direction but no lower bound on the full ground energy, compactness, continuum domain or source-owned field measure
